idea: Choose the order in which to multiply a chain of matrices so that the fewest scalar multiplications are needed. The result is the same for every order, but the cost is not. The cheapest cost of the sub-chain from i to j is the best over all split points of the two smaller chains plus the cost of joining them. Short chains are solved first.
useWhen: Planning the order of large matrix products in graphics and machine learning
Problems about the best way to bracket a sequence of operations
avoidWhen: The chain is only two or three matrices: try every order by hand
You need to multiply the matrices, not just plan the order: this only gives the plan
